scenario: A shipping-broker ranking lists only firms that remain active and grow annual commission by more than 35%. Buyers use the ranking's average to estimate typical broker growth.

data.description: Only surviving firms with growth above 35 percentage points are listed. Growth is Normal with sigma 15 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean commission-growth mu across all firms and (b) the fraction of firms listed.
naive_answer: Typical growth is about 42.6 points because that is the ranking average.
naive_trap: The ranking lists only upper-tail survivors.
reasoning_trace: Use the truncated-normal model with alpha around 1.1.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(35-mu)/15; return mu+15*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-42.59
mu=brentq(eq,-100,34.99)
frac=norm.sf((35-mu)/15)
assert abs(mu-18.5)<1 and abs(frac-0.1357)<0.005
